# Today on Hacker News

## AI/ML
The field of artificial intelligence is buzzing with activity this week. Notable posts include **[Notes from the Mistral AI Now Summit](https://koenvangilst.nl/lab/mistral-ai-now-summit)**, which highlights key discussions from a recent summit, and **[Liquid AI reveals 8B-A1B MoE trained on 38T](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-8b-a1b)**, showcasing advancements in machine learning models. Additionally, **[Shift will clean homes for free to train future robots](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/939765/ai-training-data-startup-shift-free-cleaning)** emphasizes innovative methods to gather training data for AI systems.

## Economics & Society
In the realm of economics, **[The dead economy theory](https://www.owenmcgrann.com/p/the-dead-economy-theory)** presents a thought-provoking analysis of current economic trends, while the **[California state assembly has passed the 'Protect Our Games Act'](https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/22330/stop-killing-games-movement-gains-momentum-california-assembly-passes-game-protection-bill)** raises discussions about the intersection of legislation and gaming culture.

## Technology & Development
Several posts focus on technology advancements. The article **[SQLite is all you need for durable workflows](https://obeli.sk/blog/sqlite-is-all-you-need-for-durable-workflows/)** argues for the efficiency of SQLite in various applications. Meanwhile, **[Bijou64: A variable-length integer encoding](https://www.inkandswitch.com/tangents/bijou64/)** delves into encoding techniques relevant for developers, and **[Show HN: Tiny-vLLM – high performance LLM inference engine in C++ and CUDA](https://github.com/jmaczan/tiny-vllm)** introduces a new tool for efficiently running large language models.

## Miscellaneous
In other interesting news, **[Rothko for your current weather conditions](https://rothko.joonas.wtf/)** provides a unique visual representation of the current weather, merging art and data. Additionally, **[MCP Is Dead](https://www.quandri.io/engineering-blog/mcp-is-dead)** discusses the end of a technology era, while **[It's hard to justify buying a Framework 12](https://www.jeffgeerling.com/blog/2026/its-hard-to-justify-framework-12/)** offers insights into the latest laptop models. 

Overall, this week’s Hacker News posts reflect a diverse range of topics from AI advancements to economic theories, showcasing the vibrant discussions happening in tech communities.
